Germination is slow and erratic when soil temperature is below 68 F. Fruit maturing when daily mean air temperatures are below 70 F have poorer quality. Pumpkins do well in hot weather, but very high temperatures (110-115 F) can cause temporary vine wilting, sunburned fruit, and soft fruit at harvest with reduced shelf life. Spacing depends on whether cultivars are bush or vining. Large fruited pumpkins and squash are often planted in hills 6 to 8 feet apart with rows 6 to 8 feet apart. Bush cultivars are planted at much closer spacing with in-row spacing as close as 3 feet with 6 feet between rows. Large acreages can be seeded in rows six to ten feet apart.
